quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #16
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: When changing lanes:

options.text: Only use the rearview mirror.
Look over your shoulder toward the lane you want to enter.
Only use the left side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulder toward the lane you want to enter.
questions.explanation: Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before changing lanes. Check multiple times if needed. Always watch both the traffic ahead and the traffic in the lane next to you.

questions.question: You exit the freeway on a ramp that curves downhill. You should:

options.text: Slow to a safe speed before you enter the curve.
Slow to the posted freeway speed limit.
Wait until you are in the curve to start braking.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow to a safe speed before you enter the curve.
questions.explanation: Always slow down before entering a curve. You cannot see hazards ahead in a curve. Braking inside a curve can cause your vehicle to skid.

questions.question: This sign indicates a:

options.text: Railroad crossing.
Pedestrian crossing.
No passing zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossing.
questions.explanation: Yellow signs with black markings warn drivers of upcoming hazards. Round signs warn only about railroad crossings.

questions.question: If you have an argument with another person and you are angry, you should:

options.text: Play loud music so you do not think about the argument while driving.
Wait a few minutes to calm down before driving.
Drive on the interstate to reduce your anger.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait a few minutes to calm down before driving.
questions.explanation: Anger affects your ability to drive safely. If you are very angry, excited, scared, worried, or sad, calm down before driving. You must focus on driving, not on upsetting thoughts.

questions.question: To turn left from a multilane one-way street onto another one-way street, start your turn from:

options.text: Any lane (if it is safe).
The leftmost lane.
The center lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The leftmost lane.
questions.explanation: When turning left from a one-way street to another one-way street, begin the turn from the far left lane.

questions.question: To help avoid skidding on slippery surfaces, you should:

options.text: Shift to a lower gear after you start going down a steep hill.
Speed up to enter curves and slow down to exit them.
Slow down before entering curves and intersections.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before entering curves and intersections.
questions.explanation: Slow down before entering a curve because you cannot see ahead. Braking inside a curve may cause you to skid.

questions.question: Drivers turning left must yield to:

options.text: Cars passing them.
Cars coming toward them.
No one.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cars coming toward them.
questions.explanation: A driver turning left must yield to oncoming traffic driving straight. A turning driver may only turn when it is safe and does not affect oncoming traffic.

questions.question: A driver should use the proper turn signal ____ before beginning a turn.

options.text: 50 feet
75 feet
25 feet

questions.correctAnswerText: 50 feet
questions.explanation: Turn on your signal at least 50 feet before the place where you plan to turn.

questions.question: If you want to pass a pedestrian on the roadway and an oncoming vehicle is approaching, you should:

options.text: Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass before you pass the pedestrian.
Keep driving at a steady speed. The oncoming vehicle must stop.
Honk your horn to make the pedestrian move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass before you pass the pedestrian.
questions.explanation: Handle one roadway hazard at a time when possible. If you want to pass a pedestrian but an oncoming vehicle is coming, slow down and let the vehicle pass first. Then pass the pedestrian if it is safe.

questions.question: It is illegal to make a U-turn near a curve or hill when the driver cannot:

options.text: Make the turn within 30 seconds.
See at least 500 feet in both directions.
Drive on the road shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: See at least 500 feet in both directions.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to make a U-turn anywhere you cannot clearly see at least 500 feet ahead in both directions.

questions.question: If your vehicle starts to skid, what should you do?

options.text: Ease up on the gas pedal.
Brake as hard as possible.
Turn off the ignition.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ease up on the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle skids, release the gas or brake pedal to help the vehicle balance again. Steer in the direction the back of your vehicle is sliding to regain control.

questions.question: When is it safe to return to your lane after passing another vehicle?

options.text: When you cannot see the vehicle directly to your right.
When you see the vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
When you have passed the other vehicle's front bumper.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see the vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Before moving back to your lane after passing, make sure you are far enough ahead. You can safely return to your lane when you can see both of the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: When parking next to a curb, when should you use your turn signals?

options.text: Only when pulling away from the curb.
Only when pulling next to the curb.
Both when pulling next to and away from the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both when pulling next to and away from the curb.
questions.explanation: You must signal both when you park next to a curb and when you pull away from it.

questions.question: What must you do when you see a flashing yellow light at an intersection?

options.text: Come to a complete stop.
Keep driving at normal speed.
Slow down and proceed carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means be alert and careful. Slow down when you see a flashing yellow traffic signal and proceed only when it is safe.

questions.question: How should you yield to an emergency vehicle using its siren and flashing lights?

options.text: Drive to the right edge of the road and stop.
Move into the right lane and drive slowly until it passes.
Stop immediately, even if you are in an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the right edge of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: You must yield to any emergency vehicle with its siren and lights on. Drive to the right side of the road and stop. Do not stop in an intersection. You can drive again once the emergency vehicle has passed.

questions.question: Why should you signal continuously while turning?

options.text: It is illegal to turn off your signal before completing a turn.
It tells other drivers what you plan to do.
It is always unsafe to turn off a signal before finishing a turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: It tells other drivers what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: Always signal when turning, changing lanes, slowing down, or stopping. This tells other drivers, motorcyclists, cyclists, and pedestrians what you intend to do.

questions.question: What is the purpose of work zone barriers, drums, cones, and signs?

options.text: To make drivers angry about slow traffic.
To inconvenience drivers.
To keep traffic away from dangerous work areas.

questions.correctAnswerText: To keep traffic away from dangerous work areas.
questions.explanation: Work zones are dangerous for workers and drivers. When you approach a work zone, watch for cones, barrels, signs, large vehicles, and workers in bright vests. They warn and direct you.

questions.question: What does a steady red arrow on a traffic light mean?

options.text: You cannot turn in the direction of the arrow.
You may turn in the direction of the arrow after stopping.
You may turn in the direction of the arrow.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot turn in the direction of the arrow.
questions.explanation: A steady red arrow means you cannot go in that direction. You must stop and wait for a green signal before you can proceed.

questions.question: What should you do before changing lanes besides checking your mirrors?

options.text: Never look over your right shoulder.
Always slow down in your current lane.
Look over your shoulder quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulder quickly.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to see if a vehicle is in your blind spot. Make sure no other driver is trying to enter the same lane from another direction.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: All traffic must turn right.
All traffic must go straight.
A side road is coming up ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A side road is coming up ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings and alert drivers to upcoming conditions. This sign warns you that a side road will intersect ahead, so be ready and stay alert.

questions.question: What effect does a blood alcohol concentration of 0.02 percent have?

options.text: It has no effect on your driving.
It does not put other drivers at risk.
It doubles your chances of having an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: It doubles your chances of having an accident.
questions.explanation: Every 0.02 percent increase in blood alcohol concentration nearly doubles a driver's risk of a fatal crash.

questions.question: When driving on slippery surfaces like snow or ice, what should you do?

options.text: Shift to a low gear before going down steep hills.
Stay close behind other vehicles to maintain traction.
Pump your brakes to keep them from freezing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to a low gear before going down steep hills.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, shift to a low gear before going down steep hills to prevent skidding. Follow farther behind other vehicles than normal. Avoid quick stops. Pump your brakes only if you do not have antilock brakes.

questions.question: Which statement about large trucks is true?

options.text: They take longer to stop than passenger vehicles.
All large trucks have air brakes that stop them quickly.
They are easier to steer than passenger vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They take longer to stop than passenger vehicles.
questions.explanation: Large trucks take longer to stop than other vehicles at the same speed. A passenger vehicle traveling at 55 mph can stop within 400 feet. A large truck at the same speed needs almost 800 feet to stop.

questions.question: When can you double park?

options.text: Never.
Only on a four-lane street.
When loading or unloading passengers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Double parking is against the law.

questions.question: What is true about driving too fast?

options.text: It does not increase the chance of a crash.
It improves your ability to react to hazards.
It often leads to risky decisions.

questions.correctAnswerText: It often leads to risky decisions.
questions.explanation: Excessive speed is a common cause of vehicle crashes. Speeding does not save time and often leads to risky decisions.

questions.question: What is the law about alcohol in a motor vehicle on a highway?

options.text: It is illegal to drink from or have open containers of alcohol.
It is legal to drink alcohol if you are not driving.
It is legal to drink alcohol while driving if you are not drunk.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is illegal to drink from or have open containers of alcohol.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drive under the influence of alcohol. No one in the vehicle—driver or passenger—may have an open container of alcohol while the vehicle is running.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line mean?

options.text: Vehicles in both directions may pass.
Vehicles next to the broken line may pass.
Vehicles next to the solid line may pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Vehicles next to the broken line may pass.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A broken yellow line means you may pass.

questions.question: How do sudden wind gusts affect drivers on highways?

options.text: They generally affect only large vehicles.
They only cause visibility problems.
They can affect all vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They can affect all vehicles.
questions.explanation: Strong wind affects all drivers, though it can be especially challenging for large vehicles. Wind can reduce visibility by blowing dirt and dust, and it can physically move any vehicle.

questions.question: What should a driver assume about right-of-way rules?

options.text: All drivers automatically follow right-of-way rules.
Most drivers follow right-of-way rules.
Always be ready to give up your right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always be ready to give up your right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Do not assume you have the right-of-way just because of the rules. Always think about the situation at an intersection. Be willing to yield your right-of-way if it prevents a crash.

questions.question: Hydroplaning happens when tires slide on water instead of the road. How can you prevent it in wet weather?

options.text: Use cruise control to keep a constant speed.
Slow down.
Move to the shoulder as soon as it rains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning is caused by driving too fast on wet roads. Slow down when the pavement is wet to prevent hydroplaning.
